newsitem.title: UK: Tarmac shares firm despite H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Tarmac shares firm despite H1 results.

text.p: Shares in building materials and construction services group Tarmac Plc rose with an overall stronger stock market in early trading on Tuesday despite slightly disappointing first half results, dealers said.

"There's very little in the statement or the headline numbers that was encouraging but they have performed appallingly in the run-up to the figures and the news wasn't any worse than people had feared," said one.
By 0729 GMT the shares were 4-1/2p higher at 98p.

"I'm a buyer because of the yield. The U.S. margins at eight percent are quite encouraging on the face of it. In the heavy building materials division, margins of 7-1/2 percent, down from 8.9 percent, are pretty acceptable given it includes the Wimpey business. It's not much better than expected but it is a reasonably resilient performance," said one industry analyst.

Group chief executive Neville Simms said the first half was representative neither of the true underlying performance of the businesses nor of their potential, and that the maintained interim dividend reflected the confidence of further progress in the second half and into 1997.
